description.value: The study examined sustained effects of frequent cannabis use on hippocampus-dependent associative memory using functional and structural MRI in frequent cannabis users and matched non-users.

spans.text: The purpose of the current study is to provide a comprehensive assessment of potential sustained effects of cannabis on hippocampus-dependent associative memory function.

description.value: Cross-sectional comparison of frequent cannabis users and matched non-users; participants were abstinent from cannabis and alcohol for at least 7 days before testing.

spans.text: The groups were matched for age, gender and verbal IQ.

value: The AL-SC contrast identified six regions specifically involved in associative learning: bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, right medial occipital gyrus, and bilateral parahippocampal/fusiform gyrus.

Cannabis users exhibited an overall lower magnitude of activity in these regions than controls, with hypo-activity most pronounced during associative learning in the bilateral parahippocampal area and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
